title: 1964 AHSME Problem 40
statement: A watch loses \(2\dfrac12\) minutes per day. It is set right at \(1\) P.M. on March \(15.\) Let \(n\) be the positive correction, in minutes, to be added to the time shown by the watch at a given time. When the watch shows \(9\) A.M. on March \(21,\) \(n\) equals:

solutions.text:
The watch runs at \(\frac{575}{576}\) of the correct rate. The displayed elapsed time is \(5\) days \(20\) hours, or \(8400\) minutes. Thus the real elapsed time is \(8400(\frac{576}{575}),\) and the correction is \[ \begin{aligned} n&=8400\left(\frac{576}{575}-1\right)\\ &=\frac{8400}{575} =\frac{336}{23}\\ &=14\frac{14}{23}. \end{aligned} \]

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: The watch advances \(\frac{575}{576}\) as fast as real time
From the displayed \(1\) P.M. on March \(15\) to \(9\) A.M. on March \(21\) is \(8400\) displayed minutes
